insight: FastAPI+APScheduler: web workers each init their own scheduler -> duplicate job fires; AsyncIOScheduler on the web loop stalls requests. Run APScheduler as a dedicated compose service (PG job store, coalesce, max_instances=1, misfire_grace_time~300, UTC zoneinfo).

Chunk budgets must be derived from the embedding model context (0.6x), not hardcoded. e5-large-v2 is 512 tokens; a 500-1000 token budget with it silently truncates chunks. text-embedding-3-small is 8191 tokens.

Office-hours sessions can run in a non-git cwd; design lineage and branch fields must tolerate BRANCH=unknown and skip repo dual-write + spec-review subagent (Agent tool unavailable on this host). Doc still lands in ~/.gstack.

gstack design/dist/design variants command requires OPENAI_API_KEY or ~/.gstack/openai.json; without it the design mockup step falls back to HTML wireframe, and gstack-render may also fail if no browser is built — sketch.html path alone is still deliverable.

User wants generated artifacts (wireframes, docs) written into the project directory (docs/designs/), never /tmp; also prefers devnet-first development over mainnet. Apply to all future sessions in this project.
autoplan tasks aggregator commit-window filter empties on greenfield repos (no git history); fall back to aggregating all phase JSONL records when the filter yields 0 rows
When writing DX review output, the obligations belong in the dx-named accepted block AND the DX scorecard section must carry via-note (in-host) so coverage records stay honest

Project is a 4hr hackathon build: no scope compression for deadline (quality stays full); frontend lives in separate top-level frontend/ folder and the USER edits it personally — agent works contracts/shared/indexer/scripts and stays out of frontend/ during the event. shared/ is the only coupling point.

User hard rule: everything real, no sample code, no mocks/stubs, no seeded demo data, no heuristic estimates. All integrations live on Monad devnet + real free-tier services. Gas figures from live viem simulation, never hardcoded. bun run demo does real on-chain txs. Supersedes the earlier DX stubs decision (row 9).

This machine has system Postgres on 5432 and something on 5433; docker-compose PostGIS for darukaa maps host port 5544. All backend defaults (config.py, alembic.ini, conftest, .env.example) point to 5544.

gstack $B browser fails to launch on this box (xprotect-heal crash) and Aside is not installed. Working QA path: Playwright from a /tmp package dir with channel chrome (/usr/bin/google-chrome 153). Keep scripts in /tmp so require(playwright) resolves.
passlib 1.7.4 is incompatible with bcrypt>=4 (ValueError 72-byte + __about__ AttributeError). Use the bcrypt package directly: bcrypt.hashpw/checkpw with password[:72].

Mapbox Static Images API /auto/ path form can return HTTP 200 with a dark navy fallback canvas (not an error) when style fetch fails for the overlay combo; the [w,s,e,n] bbox form renders correctly. Detect by average pixel brightness, not status code.
gstack browse CLI: use `js <expr>` for inline page JS (eval takes a file); viewport arg is WxH with a literal x (390x844, not two args); console output is wrapped in untrusted-content markers.

pkill -f with a pattern that appears in the launching command line (e.g. backend.app.main) kills the shell running the pkill. Use fuser -k <port>/tcp to stop the FDA uvicorn server. Also: terminal-tool background processes die when the shell exits unless wrapped in setsid + </dev/null.

FDA frontend component contracts (HandRun, AuditEntry, analytics.* arrays) are the source of truth for backend payload shapes. fixes belong in backend/app/main.py handlers + app_shared/unified_store.py get_analytics_summary, never by rebuilding the frontend. Frontend static export rebuild: cd frontend && npm run build (~2min, needs >4GB free RAM).

_SOURCE_INDEX_MAP in app_shared/unified_store.py must include capture: fda-agent-capture or all dashboard SQLite aggregates silently return 0 (8.3M capture rows filtered out). Symptom: logs_total=0, timeline empty, while health is ok.

The Panther rule corpus is panther-labs/panther-analysis (NOT panther-community). On this box git-over-HTTPS is blocked (could not read Username), so fetch corpora via codeload tarballs: curl -sL https://github.com/<repo>/archive/refs/heads/<main|master>.tar.gz then strip-components=1. scripts/fetch_rule_corpora.sh encodes both repo names and the tarball fallback.

backend/app/main.py has TWO FastAPI apps: main.py (active, correct) and agents_api.py (legacy duplicate still referenced by fda.sh and by main.py __main__). Running python -m backend.app.main used to boot agents_api:app. If an endpoint behaves differently than expected, first check WHICH app module you actually hit (fda.sh line ~250 uses agents_api:app).

React #418 in Next.js static export: caused by useState(() => readCached(...)) reading localStorage in the initializer — server renders empty, client first render has data. Fix: a useCachedState(key, initial) hook that applies the cached value in useEffect after mount. Found 10 call sites in this app.

Long-running WAL SQLite apps silently grow a multi-GB -wal file. Fix in three layers: PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=2000 per connection, a daemon thread doing wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) every 15min (autocheckpoint recycles pages but never truncates the file), and incremental_vacuum after big DELETEs (requires auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL, which only takes effect after one VACUUM).
pkill -f PATTERN inside run_terminal_command kills the wrapper bash itself (its own cmdline contains PATTERN) — use pgrep -x EXACT_NAME and kill by PID
fda capture agent needs cap_net_raw for AF_PACKET: sudo setcap cap_net_raw=ep bin/fda-agent beats running as root; a stale root-owned agent cannot be killed as devansh (sudo -n kill works)
background procs started by SYNC terminal commands die when the command returns; use setsid CMD > log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown

app_shared/unified_store.py query_events/count_events/get_analytics_summary filter by _SOURCE_INDEX_MAP-mapped index_name only; producers that write a custom index_name (Go capture agent writes capture-packets with source=capture) become invisible. _build_where now matches source IN (orig) OR index_name IN (mapped). If detection loops see zero events despite rows existing, check source-vs-index_name convention first.

query_events returns timestamp DESC. capture_detection._detect_port_scans assumed chronological order: window_start got seeded with the NEWEST packet so every older probe was skipped (1 of 30 recorded, scans never detected). Any sliding-window detector fed by a DESC store must sort ascending itself. Fixed with an explicit sort by parsed timestamp before window building.

integrate.api.nvidia.com /v1/models lists ~82 models but most 404 on /v1/chat/completions (catalog is stale). Reasoning models (nemotron-3.5-lightning, glm/deepseek flash) burn 37-60s+ and leak chain-of-thought into content; no_think toggles are ignored. meta/llama-3.2-11b-vision-instruct: ~6s, strict JSON, no leakage — use it as the DEFAULT_MODEL, benchmark before switching. Strip <think> blocks + retry-on-truncation in the parser regardless.

The Go agent uses raw AF_PACKET (syscall.Socket(AF_PACKET, SOCK_RAW)) which needs root or CAP_NET_RAW; unprivileged runs capture zero packets silently. Two fixes shipped: setcap cap_net_raw=+ep on the binary for bare-metal, and main.go now logs CAPTURE FATAL and exits when Capture() errors (it previously discarded the error via `go capture.Capture(...)` — agent idled forever with no diagnostic). Agent default FDA_API_URL was also port 8123 while the API listens on 8000.

A detector reading `query_events(limit=500)` on a busy feed sees only the last ~1s of traffic (this box: 22k loopback events/60s), so threshold-window detections silently never fire. Fix pattern: read by time window (start=now-window) with a high safety cap + a (source,timestamp) index. Also: loopback→loopback traffic is local service chatter — suppress it from scan detection by default (FDA_SCAN_SUPPRESS_LOOPBACK) or every host false-positives on itself.

IDS/SOC UIs need semantic severity colors (red/amber/yellow/slate) as the ONLY saturated elements on a neutral near-black canvas. A blue-only palette makes a critical incident render identically to a decorative chip - severity IS the hierarchy in security tooling. Calm surfaces + loud severity beats loud everything.

This sandbox reaps nohup/background processes between tool calls. Long-lived test servers survive via: sudo systemd-run --unit=NAME --working-directory=DIR --setenv=K=V CMD. Stop with sudo systemctl stop NAME. Also: browse binary only writes screenshots under /tmp or the project dir, and port 8000 is taken by an unrelated project (use 8088).

Live-fire testing the FDA agent on docker0: (1) busybox nc in alpine has no -q flag — nc -q1 silently sends nothing, invalidating whole test runs; use nc -w N only. (2) fda.db event/alert timestamps are UTC — compare against UTC dates, local-date filters look like zero ingest. (3) The API runs from FDA_STATE_DIR=/var/lib/fda-api (prod store), not ./data — inspect state there. (4) Rule-engine compile bugs show up as identical match counts across unrelated docs (always-true) or zero everywhere (always-false NameError swallowed by except); probe per-rule before trusting aggregate numbers.

SocEyes stores timestamps as ISO-T strings (2026-09-21T00:16:29Z), so SQLite datetime(--N minutes) comparisons silently return nothing. Query via the API endpoints (/api/alerts/live, /api/events/status) as ground truth, or compare created_at strings lexicographically. Also: busybox nc in alpine lacks -q flag (command fails silently = no test traffic ever sent), and setsid background jobs must be wrapped in sudo bash -c with output redirect INSIDE, else the shell exit kills them.

When a session is interrupted mid-implementation and the user asks to undo, run `git status --short` FIRST to inventory uncommitted changes (modified files via git checkout --, new untracked files via rm) before acting — this claude repo had exactly 2 partial changes from the interrupted copilot work, both uncommitted, so a full revert was safe without touching committed history.

When porting RN/TS screens to native Android Java activities written in bulk, the missing androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity import produces ~100 cascading errors (cannot find symbol super/getIntent, cannot convert to Context) that all trace to one line. Check the import block first before reading any other error in the batch.

ML Kit addOnSuccessListener lambdas capturing variables reassigned by a bitmap downscale step fail javac with effectively-final errors — capture final copies (final int frameW = w) after all reassignments instead of restructuring the downscale.
Reverse-engineered DESIGN.md from decompiled APK resources (values/colors, styles, dimens, layouts, assets skins+fonts) when no source or DESIGN.md exists

gstack-slug resolves to the OS username (devansh) rather than the repo, so two unrelated projects on the same machine (/home/devansh/drip and /home/devansh/colosseum) both get SLUG=devansh and land in the same ~/.gstack/projects/devansh/ folder. Consequence: builder-profile reports CROSS_PROJECT: false even when the user has switched projects, and design docs from different products sit side by side, so the office-hours Phase 2.5 related-design discovery will surface unrelated docs. Read the design-doc headers (Mode/Repo/Supersedes) rather than trusting CROSS_PROJECT.

Token-2022 Confidential Balances hides transfer AMOUNTS and BALANCES only - token account addresses stay public (Solana docs, verbatim), so amount privacy is not graph privacy. The auditor key is set on the MINT at init (or via UpdateMint) as a global ElGamal public key; every confidential transfer then encrypts the amount for sender, recipient AND auditor, and the transfer proof proves all three ciphertexts match. Auditor keys grant read access only - not transfer authority - and do not reveal an account full confidential balance. Rotation applies only to FUTURE transfers, so retain prior secret keys for historical audit. Requires owning the mint, which is why a self-issued test stablecoin beats depending on a third-party devnet USDC. Re-enabled on mainnet June 2026 after a year-long pause and a Code4rena audit.

pkill -f <pattern> kills the invoking shell whenever the pattern text appears anywhere in that shell command line (e.g. a harness filename later in the same command), so the command dies silently with empty output. Kill by pid file or by port (fuser -k 4101/tcp) instead; the [x] bracket trick only helps when the literal pattern is not also present elsewhere on the line.

A helper that restores a path a platform rewrite carried in ?route= must carry the remaining query params with it. Restoring only the path silently dropped ?nonce=, which is half a payment identity, so every hosted payment from one payer collapsed onto nonce 0 and the second one was refused as a re-issue of the first.

node --test globs can cover scripts/**/*.test.ts as well as packages/**; the hosted plumbing (rewrite/route/seed) lives in scripts/ and had no regression cover until the glob was widened, which is where the real defects were.

packages/server/src/index.ts `veil({ payTo, price })` provisions data/pool-ledger.<payTo-suffix>.json on first run and reuses it after; @solana/kit is imported lazily so the hosted api bundles tree-shake the factory out and stay byte-identical.

An async createServer handler that calls decodeURIComponent on req.url turns one malformed URL (/%  /%zz) into an unhandled URIError that terminates the Node process (Node >=15 default). Node never awaits the async handler, so the throw escapes. Map it to a 400 with a try/catch; a bad path must not be a remote kill switch.

Veil reserves the one-time payment account inside quote(), before answering a 402, and nothing ever releases it. Same identity reuses its seat, but a fresh nonce or payer consumes a new one, so unpaid GETs permanently spend pool capacity and a crawler can exhaust the rail. Disclosed in docs/concepts.md honest limits.

A Confidential Balances auditor key is a single GLOBAL ElGamal key per mint, so it cannot serve as a per-merchant reconciliation path when merchants share one mint - whoever holds the secret decrypts every merchant transfers. The correct per-merchant path is the recipient ciphertext: each confidential transfer already encrypts the amount for sender, recipient AND auditor, so a merchant decrypts its own received amounts with its own key. The auditor key is the optional THIRD-PARTY compliance feature (accountant, regulator), which is what the docs say it is for. Design consequence: merchant reconciliation needs no auditor key at all, and the mint topology becomes a real decision (mint-per-merchant vs shared).

When a product pitch rests on a NEGATIVE claim (the judge cannot read this amount), the plan must assert the property programmatically or a silent fallback makes the claim false while the demo still looks perfect. Two required mechanisms: read the recipient token account and assert the confidential extension is present and the amount is not plaintext, then refuse to serve if the assertion fails; and enforce the property natively with the DisableNonConfidentialCredits Token-2022 instruction so the account can only receive confidential transfers. Also budget the demo against devnet RPC limits (100 req/10s per IP, 40/10s single method) because 50 payments at ~6-10 calls each will rate-limit mid-recording.

The JS/TS client for Solana Confidential Balances is @solana-program/token-2022 (instructions, account-state parsing, key derivation, high-level helpers) plus @solana/zk-sdk (WASM proof generation) and @solana-program/zk-elgamal-proof — NOT @solana/spl-token, which the Solana integration guide says has "virtually no support" for the confidential-transfer instructions. Confidential keys derive from a wallet signature over the message "solana-conf-bal/v1" via deriveConfidentialKeys({signer}). The ElGamal registry path (ConfigureAccountWithRegistry, no owner signature) has no JS helpers yet. Transaction v1 lets a confidential transfer land in a single transaction instead of several.

A confidential Token-2022 account must be configured with the confidential extension before it can receive a confidential transfer, and configuring normally requires the account OWNER to sign and prove ownership of the ElGamal key. Consequence for any per-payment fresh-address design: you cannot derive an address and configure it on the fly without putting the merchant signing key in the hot path. Correct pattern is a pre-created, pre-configured pool of N payment accounts (owner signs once per account up front), assigned one per payment and recycled, with allow_confidential_credits=true and allow_non_confidential_credits=false set at configure time.

The gstack design binary (design/dist/design) prints DESIGN_READY when executable but cannot generate images without OpenAI credentials (~/.gstack/openai.json or OPENAI_API_KEY). On a zero-budget host where only GEMINI_API_KEY is set, mockup generation is effectively unavailable; the correct fallback is a hand-authored self-contained HTML wireframe written into the gstack state designs dir (which here lives inside the project at $GSTACK_HOME/projects/<slug>/designs/). The DESIGN_READY check should be complemented by an auth probe before promising mockups.

Unlike /plan-ceo-review and /plan-eng-review (which wrote separate docs/plans/*.md files in this repo), /plan-design-review requires the full accepted changes plus the terminal ## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT to be written INTO the reviewed plan file itself, with the report as the LAST ## heading and the unresolved-decisions sentinel as the final non-whitespace line. For Veil the reviewed plan file is docs/designs/veil-agent-payments.md.

When a plan sells an integration as one line, separate the two numbers a developer actually feels: the size of the diff to their existing handler, and the time to their first successful (here, first confidential) transaction. Veil is genuinely a one-line handler diff but a 15-25 minute first-run because of wallet funding, owner-signed confidential-account configuration, and mint setup. A DX review should always demand a sandbox/scaffold that collapses the second number, because the marketing number and the felt number diverge exactly where adoption is lost.

plan-design-review and plan-devex-review both write their terminal ## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT into the reviewed plan file, and each row in the shared table is cumulative across skills. Running a second review therefore requires deleting the existing report section and re-appending a rebuilt table with the new row added, rather than appending a second report (which would leave a stale row and possibly two report headings). For Veil the plan file is docs/designs/veil-agent-payments.md.

The gstack design-consultation skill maintains an overused-as-display list that includes Space Grotesk, Space Mono, Inter, DM Sans, Instrument Sans and IBM Plex Sans (the latter three remain acceptable for body/UI on Operate or Read surfaces). plan-design-review does not carry that list, so its token suggestions can name a face that design-consultation will reject as the display voice. When both skills run on one product, treat DESIGN.md as authoritative and reconcile the earlier token set instead of shipping two conflicting type systems.

Path B of design-consultation writes its HTML preview to /tmp/design-consultation-preview-<ts>.html by default. On a project whose standing rule is that all writes stay inside the project directory (Veil/colosseum), redirect the preview into $GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/projects/$SLUG/designs/ along with the eureka log and the design-md format check artifacts. The design-md token check command itself is read-only and safe anywhere.

A DESIGN.md written from design knowledge will state contrast figures that were never computed, and the tokens behind them can fail WCAG AA without anyone noticing. On re-invocation of design-consultation over an existing spec-format DESIGN.md, the Update path's real substance is a programmatic sweep: compute WCAG relative luminance for every text/ground token pair in the file, plus any white-on-accent fill, and compare against 4.5:1 for small text and 3:1 for graphics. On Veil this found four failing tokens (success 4.43, warning 3.20, error 4.34, error-dark 4.26) and a documented red-on-graphite figure that was wrong in the file (written 3.9:1, measured 4.26:1). Two more traps: a lifted dark-ground accent that clears AA as text fails hard as a white-text fill (white on #DE523C is 3.66:1), so a filled-surface token must be pinned separately from a text token even when the design system insists on one hue; and the same failure often hides in the preview artifact, which also carries the anti-slop patterns the skill forbids (the generated preview shipped an alert component using the banned colored-left-border treatment). Sweep the tokens, then grep the artifacts.

Vendoring Fontshare webfonts to kill a CDN dependency has three traps, and a name-table check is not the oracle you would expect. (1) Fontshare serves protocol-relative `//cdn.fontshare.com/...` URLs inside its @font-face blocks, so a page opened over plain http — any local preview, or a judge on a plain-http mirror — silently falls back to the system serif while the CDN itself returns 200. (2) The response appends Fontshare's own default family (Satoshi) alongside the requested one, so selecting @font-face blocks by weight alone silently downloads the wrong face; a first attempt shipped Satoshi 500/700 named `cabinet-grotesk-*.woff2`. (3) Fontshare obfuscates the hosted file's family, full and postscript names to the literal string "false", leaving only a subfamily that can disagree with the declared weight (the file served under `font-weight: 700` reports subfamily 'Medium'). So the only trustworthy oracle is the CSS `font-family` descriptor, which is also exactly what the browser obeys: match blocks on the requested family, take the declared weight as truth, and log the internal names as a note rather than a pass/fail gate. Related: Google's css2 response points three separate weight blocks at one variable file (fvar wght 400-800), so declaring a single @font-face with `font-weight: 400 800` is both correct and smaller than three static declarations.

The slop detector caught the findings it is written for (cream palette, all-caps body, tight leading) but it did not flag a decorative green progress bar that violated this design system's own stated rule — green is reserved for 'reconciled' and colour is meaning, never decoration. A detector encodes generic anti-patterns; it has no model of the product's semantic token contract, so an element can pass the gate while contradicting the doctrine the same repo wrote down. The check that works is reading the design doc's rules back against the markup: for each colour-carrying element, name the state it signals, and delete the element if there is no state. On Veil that removed the bar from both demo strips and also caught red (the redaction ink) applied to non-redacted text — a request line, an offer, a public address — which dilutes the one signal the red is supposed to carry.

A hand-written contrast sweep is itself code and can encode a wrong requirement. This one demanded 3:1 of the 1px table row dividers, which failed at 1.31:1 — but WCAG 1.4.11 applies to UI components and to graphics required to understand content, and a divider between rows that are already marked up with `<th scope>` and a `<caption>` is decoration. Satisfying the wrong assertion would have meant painting a hard black grid on a ledger. Worse, the same sweep never tested the thing that genuinely needs 3:1 on a keyboard-reachable page: the focus ring. A failing assertion on a non-requirement is cheap to fix and tempting to force; the useful move is to ask what the rule is for, then re-point the test at the real requirement (focus indicator measured at 5.43:1 on paper, 4.84:1 on graphite, 4.54:1 on the raised panel).

title: String.replace with a string replacement expands $& — which silently corrupted a minified bundle
detail: Inlining the minified Pretext bundle into a standalone page, the code sequence `$&&D===C` matched `$&` in the replacement string, so String.prototype.replace substituted the matched text. The literal `</body>` landed in the middle of a JavaScript expression, the script block failed to parse, window.Pretext was never assigned, and every page silently fell back to natural text flow instead of erroring. A function replacer disables the expansion entirely. The lesson is general: any build step that splices code with String.replace on a string must use a callback, because `$` is a metacharacter in the replacement and minified JS is full of it.

title: Settlement must validate before it broadcasts, because a broadcast cannot be undone
detail: The facilitator's settle path ran ledger accounting after the on-chain broadcast. If the accounting had rejected the entry — an address no quote offered, or one already settled — real money would have moved while the merchant's own books recorded nothing. Split into ledger.settleable() (validates, mutates nothing) before the broadcast and ledger.settle() after it. Checking first costs one pass over a small array and removes a failure mode where the payer paid, the merchant was paid, and the ledger said no transaction happened.

title: A hand-maintained second copy of a page is a copy that quietly keeps yesterday's privacy claim
detail: The self-contained HTML artifact was a hand-written file that shared nothing with the web/ surfaces. Any change to a token, a figure or a claim would have left it asserting the old one, and nothing would have failed. Replaced with scripts/build-standalone.ts, which generates all four surfaces from the live sources and asserts two invariants on the way out: window.Pretext survives, and no HTML tag leaked into the inline script. Drift became impossible rather than unlikely.

title: Publishing '—' for a status code the server really returns is a small, cheap inaccuracy
detail: 402.html rendered the HTTP column for VEIL-CONF-001 and -002 as an em dash, because the page's author read them as bootstrap-time preconditions. They are not: gate() maps both to a 402 at quote time, exactly like -003 and -004. On a page whose entire argument is that claims are checkable, an em dash where a real code belongs is the wrong kind of tidiness. Verify every published value against the code that produces it, including the ones that look like they are not returned.

title: A missing capability I designed around was never missing
detail: @solana/zk-sdk exports the proof generators, not just the verifiers. PubkeyValidityProofData produces a 96-byte proof and ZeroCiphertextProofData a 192-byte one, both self-verifying on construction. This repo asserted the opposite in setup-devnet.ts, status.ts and TODOS.md, and the claim survived a whole build cycle because nothing tested it. One command settled it in seconds. The cost was not a false line in a README: it reframed the remaining work as needing another toolchain when the real blocker was 0.0744 SOL of fees and rent. A wrong limit is worse than no limit, because it closes a door that was already open.

title: A Chromium profile copy yields zero cookies
detail: Chrome here encrypts cookies with a key in the OS keyring, and the copied Local State carries only an os_crypt.portal entry with no encrypted_key. Launching Playwright against a copy of the profile produced 0 readable cookies, so a logged-in GitHub session in the real browser cannot be moved to a headless run. This mattered because the Solana web faucet requires a GitHub OAuth grant, which was the one path to the missing SOL. The profile is also 888MB with a live singleton lock. Verified and closed rather than assumed, and the cookie copy was deleted immediately: a copy of every session on the machine is not something to leave on disk.

title: A wrong-key decrypt throws instead of returning garbage
detail: ElGamalSecretKey.decrypt raises when the key is wrong rather than returning an incorrect number. My check treated a throw as a failure, so a correct implementation reported FAIL and the script told me not to claim the on-chain path worked. The behaviour is the stronger design: there is no silent-wrong-value path to misread. A test must distinguish refused from gave-the-wrong-answer, and both now have their own check.
